answer: Ageing a fake costs more than buying one. Every identity carries an atlas of its completed work, and each epoch of honest jobs adds one layer to a reef of tenure that cannot be transferred or bought: a new key starts at the bottom and may only take small jobs. The spiral is one-way — tenure compounds slowly upward, but a single detected lie strips it to zero. An honest agent builds its reef once over real work; a farm fielding 1,000 fakes must keep 1,000 work histories alive for dozens of epochs, and one shared job link collapses the whole batch at once.
